title: Business Strategy
tagline: Rings by weight: the decision sits at the centre, everything else earns its distance.

clusters.label: Decisions
clusters.summary: The unit of value in strategy work.

clusters.label: Measurement
clusters.summary: Knowing whether any of it worked.

nodes.label: Decision quality
nodes.summary: Judge a process by the quality of the decision it produced, separately from the outcome it got.
keyPoints: Name the decision, its owner, its cadence, and the cost of being wrong.
Good decisions can have bad outcomes; a process that can't tell them apart learns nothing.
Analytics earns its keep only where it changes what someone does.

nodes.label: Problem framing
nodes.summary: Most strategy errors are framing errors: the right answer to a question nobody needed answered.
keyPoints: State the alternative you are choosing against — a strategy with no rejected option is a wish.
Separate reversible bets from one-way doors and spend review time accordingly.
Write the disconfirming evidence you would accept, in advance.

nodes.label: Trade-offs & constraints
nodes.summary: Strategy is the set of things you have decided not to do, made explicit.
keyPoints: Every 'and also' silently reduces the odds on everything already committed.
Constraints are more useful than goals for guiding day-to-day choices.
Sequencing is a trade-off too: what gets postponed is part of the plan.

nodes.label: Operating model
nodes.summary: The recurring meetings, owners, and interfaces that carry a strategy between quarters.
keyPoints: Structure follows the decisions that need to be made repeatedly.
An unowned initiative is a stated preference, not a plan.
Interfaces between teams are where most execution latency accumulates.

nodes.label: Strategy to execution
nodes.summary: The translation layer from a written intent to what teams actually pick up on Monday.
keyPoints: Translate intent into a small number of visible commitments.
Review cadence should match how fast the underlying evidence changes.
When plans and behaviour disagree, believe the behaviour.

nodes.label: Prioritisation
nodes.summary: Ranking work by expected decision value rather than by whoever asked most recently.
keyPoints: Score by the decision it improves and the cost of delay.
A backlog without a stopping rule is a queue, not a priority list.
Capacity is the constraint people most often refuse to state.

nodes.label: Measurement design
nodes.summary: Choose the smallest set of metrics that would actually change a decision if they moved.
keyPoints: Every metric needs an owner, a grain, and a defined response when it moves.
Leading indicators are guesses about causality — label them as such.
A metric that nobody would act on is reporting, not measurement.

resources.label: Sessionize event data
resources.note: Defining the behaviour a metric counts

nodes.label: Evidence & experiments
nodes.summary: Deciding how much confidence a piece of evidence deserves before it moves a plan.
keyPoints: Match the method to the stakes: a two-week test does not justify a five-year commitment.
Pre-register the threshold that would change your mind.
Most strategic evidence is observational; say so instead of dressing it as causal.

nodes.label: Narrative & alignment
nodes.summary: The version of the strategy people can repeat correctly without the document in front of them.
keyPoints: If it can't be repeated in two sentences, it won't survive delegation.
Alignment is tested by what people decline, not by what they applaud.
Repeat the same framing until it is boring to you — that is roughly when it lands.
